_doc: Lyle Boggs, deckhand on the towboat Kanawha Belle. He was under the Silver Bridge in November 1966 and in December 1967. He wants to talk and will not say so.

open.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: You're the ones from the Office. Deputy said. He said be polite, so this is me being polite.
He's splicing a line and not looking at us.

passives.line: He looks at the river between every word. Not at you. He's checking it's still there.
That line is already spliced. Busy hands, nothing to do. He wants to talk and he wants it to be your idea.

options.text: We can come back when the Belle's tied up.
You're being polite like a man who's been told to.
The deputy also said you saw something in '66.

menu.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: Ask. I've got till the ice lets go of the barge.

static.line: He already knows what you're going to ask. Ask the other thing.

options.text: What did you see in November '66?
(Look at the gap where the bridge was.)
The Belle crosses every morning. Nobody would count four more on the barge.
June wants to know about the long antenna on your boat.

lights.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: November '66. Night tow, downbound, coming under the bridge. Two red lights on the water ahead of us, low, where a boat's lights would be.
No bow light. No stern light. And they were going upstream. Against the current. Nothing goes against this current without a diesel, and I'd have heard a diesel.
Skipper put the spot on them. There wasn't anything there to put a spot on. The lights went up the bank and went out.

passives.line: Two lights, no running lights, against the current. Not a boat. Not a bird, either, he's leaving that word out on purpose.

options.text: Two red lights going the wrong way, and you finished the tow?

told.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: Told the Register. They had a crane man by then, so I was a crane man too, in the paper. I'm not a crane man.
Told the deputy. He bought shells. I finished the tow because the tow doesn't care what I saw.
Write the lights down exactly like he said it. Low, red, upstream.

bridge.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: December fifteenth, '67. We were tied up right there, under it, waiting on the lock. Five o'clock, rush hour, the bridge full both ways.
It made a noise like a chain going through a hawsehole. Then it was in the river with us.

passives.line: He's never said the word 'fell'. Not once. 'The bridge went.' Like a dog goes.

static.line: He was under it. He was under it and he's going to tell you it was quick. Don't let him.

bridge_quiet.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: ...All afternoon the radio had been doing a thing. Channel 16. Three notes and a quiet and three notes. Skipper said Gallipolis was testing something.
It stopped when the bridge went. I noticed that. I noticed that before I noticed anything else, and I've never told anybody, because what kind of a man notices the radio.
The kind who was listening. That's all. The kind who was listening.

bridge_pulled.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: One. A woman off the Ohio side, in a green coat, and I got her over the gunwale and she wasn't even cold yet.
She asked me were the birds still there. I said what birds. She said the ones on the cable, the big ones, the ones that were sitting on the cable when it went.
There weren't any birds on the cable. I'd been looking at that bridge all afternoon. There weren't any birds.
...She saw them. He didn't. Both of those are true.

bridge_shut.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: No. No, we're not doing that one. You can have the lights and you can have the river. You don't get that.

ferry_yes.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: First light. We cross for the Ohio-side mail and a crewman. You stand on the barge, you hold the rail, you don't touch anything, and you don't tell the company.
You miss first light, you wait for tomorrow. The river doesn't do afternoons.
Gallipolis by boat. Gus Weller's car was found in Gallipolis.

ferry_no.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: Company boat. Company rules. You want across, there's a bridge now, and I hear it's a good one.
He'll come round. Men who say 'company rules' never mean it the second time.

radio.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: The long whip on the cabin roof. That's not a marine antenna.
No, ma'am. That's mine. Channel 16, every night, and a logbook since '67. Company thinks it's for weather.

options.text: Show her the log for December '67. She'll know what she's looking at.

radio_log.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: ...Page one. December fifteenth, 1967. 1600 hours: three tones, channel 16, repeating. 1704: stopped.
Page two is January. There's a lot of pages. It's come back twice. November of '76, and this week.
This week. Lyle, what time this week?
Every night since you people came to town. Starts about the time the gate shuts.

radio_why.speaker: rf_deckhand
lines: That's all. For it to stop, and for me to be listening when it does.
